raw_response:
I’m an old hand at this, so I won’t do anything fancy. On my 13.1 mu I’ll still do wheat and maize in the usual wheat-maize rotation. That’s what suits our land here, and with only two people at home and some off-farm work, I can’t manage something too troublesome. I mostly do what has worked on my own fields. Wheat still needs enough base fertilizer and a couple of waterings if the year turns dry, otherwise it won’t tiller well. Maize goes in right after wheat harvest, fast, no delay. The gap is short, so I won’t do heavy tillage, just quick field prep and sow. Fertilizer also has to be in round, practical amounts. I’d rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than let the crop go hungry, but I still have to keep cash in hand, so I won’t push too hard. If I see insects or too many weeds, then I spray. If not, I don’t waste money.
